64	[00:06:41] Kerem Yalçın: ...no, it's fine, the other meeting ran late, sorry. Can everyone hear me?
65	[00:06:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, loud and clear.
66	[00:06:45] Burcu Tan: You're a bit echoey Kerem.
67	[00:06:47] Kerem Yalçın: Hm. Better? I switched to the headset.
68	[00:06:49] Burcu Tan: Better, yes.
69	[00:06:51] Selin Aydın: Okay so, um, I'll share my screen. Can you see the document? The statement debt one, the September analysis.
70	[00:06:58] Ozan Er: Yes, we see it.
71	[00:07:00] Selin Aydın: Good. So I put the open points in yellow, there are, let me count, eleven? Twelve. We don't have to do all of them today but the edge cases I really want to close because Deniz's team is already building.
72	[00:07:13] Deniz Arı: Yes, that would help a lot. Most of our questions are in the edge case part anyway. The happy path is quite clear.
73	[00:07:20] Selin Aydın: Okay. Then let's start with, um, silence. Because that one I wrote quickly and I'm not happy with it.
74	[00:07:27] Selin Aydın: Right now it says if the customer is silent three times, we go to the main menu.
75	[00:07:32] Kerem Yalçın: That's what we agreed in September, no?
76	[00:07:34] Selin Aydın: That's what I wrote, yes.
77	[00:07:36] Kerem Yalçın: I think it's fine. Main menu, they can choose something else there.
78	[00:07:40] Ozan Er: Can I ask one thing about the first two? What does the assistant do on the first silence? Because the document only talks about the third.
79	[00:07:47] Selin Aydın: Ah. Good point. It repeats the question, I'd say.
80	[00:07:50] Ozan Er: The whole question or a short version?
81	[00:07:53] Selin Aydın: Short. Like, it asked which card, the customer says nothing, it asks again shorter. Not the whole sentence with the examples.
82	[00:08:00] Ozan Er: Okay, so silence one, short repeat. Silence two, short repeat. Silence three...
83	[00:08:05] Kerem Yalçın: Main menu. Let's keep it, we can come back if Burcu has something.
84	[00:08:09] Burcu Tan: I have something but let me check it first, I'm not sure what the IVR does today exactly. I'll look while you continue.
85	[00:08:15] Kerem Yalçın: Okay.
86	[00:08:17] Selin Aydın: Next one. Unclear answer. Or the customer refuses to give the information, like we ask the last four digits and they say "why do you need it", that kind of thing.
87	[00:08:26] Deniz Arı: For us these are the same branch. The question is asked again and the customer gets three tries. After three, main menu. Is that okay?
88	[00:08:33] Selin Aydın: Three tries per question, yes. That matches what we do in the IVR.
89	[00:08:37] Burcu Tan: Yes, three. [inaudible] ...the IVR also counts per menu, not per call.
90	[00:08:42] Ozan Er: Per question then. And if the customer just asks to hear it again, like "can you repeat the amount", that doesn't count as a try, right?
91	[00:08:49] Selin Aydın: No, no. Repeating is not a failure. They can ask as many times as they want.
92	[00:08:53] Ozan Er: Okay. And what does it say when the three tries are gone? Because in the document there's, um, there's a sentence at the bottom of the exit table.
93	[00:09:00] Selin Aydın: Yes, I wrote "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum."
94	[00:09:04] Burcu Tan: The IVR says "aktarıyorum". Not "yönlendiriyorum". We had a whole discussion about that two years ago, I don't want to start it again [laughs].
95	[00:09:11] Kerem Yalçın: And I think it should say why. Not just "I'm transferring you". The customer tried three times, they should hear that we can't help right now.
96	[00:09:18] Deniz Arı: So something like "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" and then the transfer?
97	[00:09:22] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Selin, can you write it full?
98	[00:09:25] Selin Aydın: Typing. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Two sentences.
99	[00:09:31] Burcu Tan: That's good. That's close to the IVR line.
100	[00:09:33] Ozan Er: And for the normal end, when the customer says "no, nothing else, thanks"? Same sentence?
101	[00:09:38] Kerem Yalçın: No, there nothing went wrong. There it's just the transfer.
102	[00:09:42] Selin Aydın: For the normal end I'd keep "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now. When the call routing project comes we look at all these sentences together anyway.
103	[00:09:50] Burcu Tan: Fine for me, as long as the failure one says "aktarıyorum".
104	[00:09:53] Deniz Arı: Noted. Failure after three tries: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Normal end stays as it is in the document.
105	[00:10:01] Selin Aydın: Yes.
106	[00:10:03] Kerem Yalçın: Can someone close the door, there's a delivery guy shouting outside here.
107	[00:10:07] Burcu Tan: That's on your side Kerem [laughs].
108	[00:10:09] Kerem Yalçın: Ah, yes, sorry. One second. [inaudible]
109	[00:10:20] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Go on.
110	[00:10:22] Selin Aydın: Non-Turkish. Customer speaks English or Arabic or German, whatever.
111	[00:10:27] Deniz Arı: We assume this flow answers only in Turkish?
112	[00:10:30] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. For now only Turkish. There is an English menu in the IVR, they can go from the main menu.
113	[00:10:36] Ozan Er: So it doesn't answer the question, it just transfers. What does it say? Turkish, I assume, since the call is Turkish.
114	[00:10:42] Burcu Tan: Just "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Nothing else. They won't understand a long sentence anyway.
115	[00:10:47] Selin Aydın: Okay. "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." for non-Turkish. Writing.
116	[00:10:52] Deniz Arı: Good.
117	[00:10:54] Selin Aydın: Out of scope next. So in the document I wrote out of scope goes directly to the main menu.
118	[00:11:00] Deniz Arı: Yes, that's one we wanted to discuss. Ozan, you had the example from the tests.
119	[00:11:05] Ozan Er: Yes. So we tried it like that and the problem is, the customer asks something small, like, um, "what is my card limit" in the middle of the card selection, and boom, they're in the main menu. They didn't want to leave, they just asked something.
120	[00:11:18] Kerem Yalçın: Hm.
121	[00:11:19] Ozan Er: So our proposal: the assistant says it can't help with that, and asks if they want to go to the main menu. If yes, main menu. If they want to continue, back to where they were.
122	[00:11:28] Kerem Yalçın: I like that. Selin?
123	[00:11:30] Selin Aydın: Yes, I'm okay. What is the sentence exactly?
124	[00:11:33] Ozan Er: We had something like "Bu konuda size yardımcı olamıyorum, ana menüye..." uh, I don't remember our wording.
125	[00:11:39] Kerem Yalçın: Let's make it consistent with the one we just wrote. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" style.
126	[00:11:45] Selin Aydın: So: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?"
127	[00:11:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, that sounds natural.
128	[00:11:53] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Keep it.
129	[00:11:55] Deniz Arı: And if the answer to that question is unclear? Like they say "hmm, well, I don't know"?
130	[00:12:00] Selin Aydın: Same as every other question. Ask again, three tries.
131	[00:12:04] Deniz Arı: And after three, the failure sentence and main menu.
132	[00:12:07] Selin Aydın: Yes.
133	[00:12:08] Ozan Er: Good, I'm writing it in our sheet. Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.
134	[00:12:20] Kerem Yalçın: Wait, payment is not out of scope in that sense. If someone wants to pay, that goes to an agent, we said it in the e-mails.
135	[00:12:27] Deniz Arı: Yes, yes, payment is separate. Payment and disputes go to an agent. This is only for things that have nothing to do with the statement.
136	[00:12:33] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Just so it's clear.
137	[00:12:35] Selin Aydın: Next, the angry customer. In the document: one calming reply, then agent.
138	[00:12:41] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, that's fine I think. We don't want the bot arguing with an angry customer.
139	[00:12:46] Deniz Arı: Okay. One calming sentence and then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
140	[00:12:51] Ozan Er: And insults, we don't answer the insult itself, right? It just stays polite.
141	[00:12:55] Kerem Yalçın: Never answers the insult. Stays polite, yes.
142	[00:12:58] Selin Aydın: Okay, that one stays as written then.
143	[00:13:01] Selin Aydın: Card selection. This is the long one. Mert isn't here but I talked to him yesterday.
144	[00:13:07] Deniz Arı: Okay, go.
145	[00:13:09] Selin Aydın: So. The customer has two cards with the same name. Two Yıldız cards, for example. We ask the last four digits.
146	[00:13:17] Ozan Er: And the question is "Yıldız isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?" That one we have from your document, yes.
147	[00:13:24] Selin Aydın: Yes. Now, what if the last four are also the same? It's rare but it happens, with renewed cards, or, um, with some business customers.
148	[00:13:33] Kerem Yalçın: How rare?
149	[00:13:35] Selin Aydın: I don't have a number. Mert said it exists.
150	[00:13:38] Kerem Yalçın: Okay.
151	[00:13:39] Selin Aydın: In the document I wrote: if the last four are the same, ask the full card number.
152	[00:13:44] Deniz Arı: We'd prefer one step in between. Last six digits. Most people can read six digits off the card without trouble, the full number is sixteen digits, people make mistakes, and saying the full number on the phone, some customers don't like it.
153	[00:13:56] Elçin Ural: Sorry, I'm joining late. Hello everyone. What are we on?
154	[00:13:59] Selin Aydın: Hi Elçin. Card selection, two cards same last four digits.
155	[00:14:03] Elçin Ural: Ah okay. Go on, I'll catch up.
156	[00:14:05] Deniz Arı: So, last four, then last six, then only if the last six are also the same, the full card number.
157	[00:14:12] Elçin Ural: From my side it's better if we ask less of the number. Six instead of sixteen, yes, fine.
158	[00:14:17] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, I'm fine. Selin, sentences?
159	[00:14:20] Selin Aydın: Um. For the six. "Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?" With the real four digits of course, I just put the ones from the test card.
160	[00:14:33] Ozan Er: Yes, the digits come from the service. And for the full number?
161	[00:14:37] Selin Aydın: "Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?"
162	[00:14:43] Ozan Er: Okay. And the digits, when the assistant says "4253" it's digit by digit. Dört, iki, beş, üç. Not "kırk iki elli üç".
163	[00:14:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR also reads digit by digit.
164	[00:14:54] Elçin Ural: And it never reads the full number back. Even if the customer says it.
165	[00:14:58] Deniz Arı: Never. It doesn't repeat what the customer said either, it just goes to the debt of that card.
166	[00:15:03] Elçin Ural: Good.
167	[00:15:05] Selin Aydın: Okay. I'll ask Deniz to add the six-digit step as a comment in my document, I'll put it in properly later.
168	[00:15:11] Deniz Arı: Sure, I'll do it after the call.
169	[00:15:13] Burcu Tan: Can I go back to silence? I checked.
170	[00:15:16] Selin Aydın: Yes, go.
171	[00:15:17] Burcu Tan: So in the IVR today, after the third no-input, we don't send them to the main menu. We hang up. There's a sentence, then disconnect.
172	[00:15:25] Kerem Yalçın: Really? I thought it went back to the menu.
173	[00:15:28] Burcu Tan: Only in the main menu itself it loops once. In the sub-menus after three no-inputs, it's goodbye. The logic is, if we can't hear the customer three times, either the line is broken or they left the phone. Sending them to the menu is just more silence.
174	[00:15:42] Deniz Arı: That makes sense for us too. If there's nobody there, the main menu will also time out.
175	[00:15:47] Kerem Yalçın: Okay, then let's do the same. Hang up.
176	[00:15:50] Elçin Ural: The customer should hear why the call is ending. Not just click.
177	[00:15:54] Burcu Tan: Yes, the IVR says it. Let me find the exact line... um. It's something about not hearing the caller, I don't have it word for word.
178	[00:16:01] Ozan Er: For a voice assistant I'd say "alamadığım". Like, the problem is we're not receiving the voice, it's not the customer's fault.
179	[00:16:07] Selin Aydın: "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." Like that?
180	[00:16:12] Burcu Tan: Yes, that's fine. Better than ours actually.
181	[00:16:15] Elçin Ural: Fine for me.
182	[00:16:16] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Decided. Three silences: first two short repeat, third "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and hang up. Not main menu.
183	[00:16:25] Deniz Arı: Got it. And we said the first two are just a short repeat of the question.
184	[00:16:29] Selin Aydın: Yes. I'll fix the document.
185	[00:16:31] Deniz Arı: The timing, how many seconds is a silence, that we can leave for another day I think. We have a default.
186	[00:16:37] Burcu Tan: Let's leave it. I'll send you what the IVR uses.
187	[00:16:40] Selin Aydın: Okay. Now, Elçin, since you're here. Currencies. Kerem, this one was for you two.
188	[00:16:46] Elçin Ural: Yes, I saw the comment. The reading of the currency names?
189	[00:16:50] Selin Aydın: Yes. So in my table, the sentences for the currencies without debt, I wrote "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", "USD borcunuz bulunmamaktadır" and so on, because it was shorter to type.
190	[00:17:01] Ozan Er: And the assistant would literally say "te le" or "u se de". That's the problem. The text-to-speech reads what we give it.
191	[00:17:07] Elçin Ural: No, no abbreviations to the customer. The customer has to hear the currency name in full.
192	[00:17:12] Kerem Yalçın: Agreed.
193	[00:17:13] Selin Aydın: So: "Türk Lirası", "Dolar", "Euro", "İngiliz Sterlini".
194	[00:17:18] Elçin Ural: Yes. TL is Türk Lirası, USD is Dolar, EUR is Euro, GBP is İngiliz Sterlini. Always.
195	[00:17:24] Deniz Arı: Also in the combined sentence. So "Türk Lirası borcunuz bulunmamaktadır", not "TL borcunuz bulunmamaktadır".
196	[00:17:31] Elçin Ural: Yes. Everywhere it speaks.
197	[00:17:33] Ozan Er: And "Euro" stays "Euro", not "Avro"?
198	[00:17:36] Elçin Ural: Euro. That's what we use in all customer communication.
199	[00:17:39] Kerem Yalçın: And İngiliz Sterlini, not just "Sterlin", not "pound".
200	[00:17:43] Elçin Ural: İngiliz Sterlini, yes.
201	[00:17:45] Selin Aydın: Okay, I'll change the table. It's fifteen rows, I'll do it tonight.
202	[00:17:49] Deniz Arı: We'll read them in full on our side anyway, whatever the table says.
203	[00:17:53] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Still, I'll fix it.
204	[00:17:56] Burcu Tan: Is someone's mic open? There's typing.

291	[00:25:40] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Selin, you'll fix the document?
292	[00:25:43] Selin Aydın: I'll fix what I can by tomorrow. The edge case section I'll redo anyway, it's a mess.
293	[00:25:51] Deniz Arı: I'll send it, maybe not today, tomorrow or Friday.

Statement debt analysis session - Freya Bank / Freya
Wednesday 7 October 2026, 14:30, video call
Recording: automatic transcript, excerpt. Speaker detection may be wrong where people talk over each other.
Participants: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan, Elçin Ural (joined at about 00:14), Deniz Arı, Ozan Er

[...]

[00:01:12] Selin Aydın: ...okay, I think it's recording now. Kerem is in another call, he said five minutes.
[00:01:17] Burcu Tan: Then it's ten minutes [laughs].
[00:01:19] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Probably. Deniz, Ozan, can you hear me fine?
[00:01:22] Deniz Arı: Yes. Hi Selin, hi Burcu.
[00:01:24] Ozan Er: Hi. Sorry, my camera is off, the internet here is a bit weak today.
[00:01:28] Burcu Tan: Are you at the office?
[00:01:29] Ozan Er: No, at home, the building is doing something with the cables. Since Monday.
[00:01:33] Burcu Tan: Ours was like that last year, three weeks. Good luck.
[00:01:36] Selin Aydın: Okay. While we wait for Kerem, maybe two small things on the reading part? Those don't need him.
[00:01:42] Deniz Arı: Sure. We had a few small ones too.
[00:01:45] Selin Aydın: First, the order. When a card has debt in more than one currency. I wrote Türk Lirası first, then the foreign currencies. Is that clear enough in the document?
[00:01:54] Ozan Er: Mostly. We read it as: the card intro with the statement date, then Türk Lirası, then Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini in that order, then one sentence for all the currencies with no debt, then the due date.
[00:02:06] Selin Aydın: Yes, exactly that.
[00:02:08] Ozan Er: And the remaining automatic payment, if there is one, before the due date.
[00:02:12] Selin Aydın: Yes. Before the due date.
[00:02:14] Burcu Tan: The IVR reads the due date last too. People remember the last thing they hear.
[00:02:18] Deniz Arı: Makes sense.
[00:02:20] Ozan Er: Then for the due date the sentence is "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi]'dir." with the date like "21 Ekim 2025". Day, month name, year.
[00:02:30] Selin Aydın: Yes. And if the due date is today, it should say today. Not the date.
[00:02:35] Ozan Er: "Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür." Okay, we have that.
[00:02:39] Selin Aydın: Good.
[00:02:41] Deniz Arı: Second small one from us. After the debt is read, if the customer has more than one card, what comes first, the other-card question or the offer? E-mail and the week change.
[00:02:51] Selin Aydın: Hm. I'd say other card first. The customer called for the debt. If they have another card, maybe they want that one too.
[00:02:58] Deniz Arı: So: "Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?" and only when the cards are done, or they say no, the offer.
[00:03:05] Selin Aydın: Yes. Let's confirm with Kerem but I think he'll agree.
[00:03:09] Burcu Tan: And if they have only one card, you don't ask the other-card question, obviously.
[00:03:13] Deniz Arı: No, then straight to the offer.
[00:03:15] Ozan Er: And the offer only has what the customer can actually do. That's why we keep asking about the e-mail and the yearly right, it's connected.
[00:03:21] Selin Aydın: Yes, we'll get to that, it's in the yellow list.
[00:03:24] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:03:26] Deniz Arı: The amounts, that's clear, I think. Lira and kuruş in full, like "bin iki yüz lira elli kuruş", and if kuruş is zero we don't say "sıfır kuruş".
[00:03:35] Selin Aydın: Yes. And the foreign currencies with cents. Sterlin with pence, um, "peni".
[00:03:40] Ozan Er: Yes, we did that already.
[00:03:42] Burcu Tan: Can I ask something off topic, sorry. Selin, the training on Thursday, is it still on?
[00:03:47] Selin Aydın: Which one? The onboarding group?
[00:03:49] Burcu Tan: The onboarding group, yes. I have two people starting.
[00:03:52] Selin Aydın: I think so. I'll check and write you.
[00:03:54] Burcu Tan: Thanks.
[00:03:56] Ozan Er: One more on the card question. The example card names in "Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, [kart adı] veya [kart adı] diyebilirsiniz." Those are the customer's own cards, max two, right?
[00:04:07] Selin Aydın: Yes. Never a card the customer doesn't have. It would confuse them.
[00:04:11] Ozan Er: Okay.
[00:04:12] Deniz Arı: And after the customer picks the card, we go to the debt. No "okay, continuing with your Yıldız card" sentence.
[00:04:18] Selin Aydın: No, that's not needed. The card name is in the first sentence of the reading anyway.
[00:04:23] Deniz Arı: Exactly.
[00:04:24] Selin Aydın: Okay. Let me open the edge cases, so we're ready when Kerem joins. Let me just... the sharing is not... one second.
[00:04:31] Burcu Tan: We see your mail.
[00:04:33] Selin Aydın: Oops. Okay. Now?
[00:04:35] Burcu Tan: Now a white page.
[00:04:37] Selin Aydın: It's loading. The file is big.
[00:04:40] Ozan Er: [inaudible] ...every time.
[00:04:43] Selin Aydın: Sorry?
[00:04:44] Ozan Er: Nothing, I said the same happens to me every time with that tool.
[00:04:48] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Okay. I'll stop sharing until Kerem is in.

[...]

[00:06:41] Kerem Yalçın: ...no, it's fine, the other meeting ran late, sorry. Can everyone hear me?
[00:06:44] Deniz Arı: Yes, loud and clear.
[00:06:45] Burcu Tan: You're a bit echoey Kerem.
[00:06:47] Kerem Yalçın: Hm. Better? I switched to the headset.
[00:06:49] Burcu Tan: Better, yes.
[00:06:51] Selin Aydın: Okay so, um, I'll share my screen. Can you see the document? The statement debt one, the September analysis.
[00:06:58] Ozan Er: Yes, we see it.
[00:07:00] Selin Aydın: Good. So I put the open points in yellow, there are, let me count, eleven? Twelve. We don't have to do all of them today but the edge cases I really want to close because Deniz's team is already building.
[00:07:13] Deniz Arı: Yes, that would help a lot. Most of our questions are in the edge case part anyway. The happy path is quite clear.
[00:07:20] Selin Aydın: Okay. Then let's start with, um, silence. Because that one I wrote quickly and I'm not happy with it.
[00:07:27] Selin Aydın: Right now it says if the customer is silent three times, we go to the main menu.
[00:07:32] Kerem Yalçın: That's what we agreed in September, no?
[00:07:34] Selin Aydın: That's what I wrote, yes.
[00:07:36] Kerem Yalçın: I think it's fine. Main menu, they can choose something else there.
[00:07:40] Ozan Er: Can I ask one thing about the first two? What does the assistant do on the first silence? Because the document only talks about the third.
[00:07:47] Selin Aydın: Ah. Good point. It repeats the question, I'd say.
[00:07:50] Ozan Er: The whole question or a short version?
[00:07:53] Selin Aydın: Short. Like, it asked which card, the customer says nothing, it asks again shorter. Not the whole sentence with the examples.
[00:08:00] Ozan Er: Okay, so silence one, short repeat. Silence two, short repeat. Silence three...
[00:08:05] Kerem Yalçın: Main menu. Let's keep it, we can come back if Burcu has something.
[00:08:09] Burcu Tan: I have something but let me check it first, I'm not sure what the IVR does today exactly. I'll look while you continue.
[00:08:15] Kerem Yalçın: Okay.
[00:08:17] Selin Aydın: Next one. Unclear answer. Or the customer refuses to give the information, like we ask the last four digits and they say "why do you need it", that kind of thing.
[00:08:26] Deniz Arı: For us these are the same branch. The question is asked again and the customer gets three tries. After three, main menu. Is that okay?
[00:08:33] Selin Aydın: Three tries per question, yes. That matches what we do in the IVR.
[00:08:37] Burcu Tan: Yes, three. [inaudible] ...the IVR also counts per menu, not per call.
[00:08:42] Ozan Er: Per question then. And if the customer just asks to hear it again, like "can you repeat the amount", that doesn't count as a try, right?
[00:08:49] Selin Aydın: No, no. Repeating is not a failure. They can ask as many times as they want.
[00:08:53] Ozan Er: Okay. And what does it say when the three tries are gone? Because in the document there's, um, there's a sentence at the bottom of the exit table.
[00:09:00] Selin Aydın: Yes, I wrote "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum."
[00:09:04] Burcu Tan: The IVR says "aktarıyorum". Not "yönlendiriyorum". We had a whole discussion about that two years ago, I don't want to start it again [laughs].
[00:09:11] Kerem Yalçın: And I think it should say why. Not just "I'm transferring you". The customer tried three times, they should hear that we can't help right now.
[00:09:18] Deniz Arı: So something like "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" and then the transfer?
[00:09:22] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. Selin, can you write it full?
[00:09:25] Selin Aydın: Typing. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Two sentences.
[00:09:31] Burcu Tan: That's good. That's close to the IVR line.
[00:09:33] Ozan Er: And for the normal end, when the customer says "no, nothing else, thanks"? Same sentence?
[00:09:38] Kerem Yalçın: No, there nothing went wrong. There it's just the transfer.
[00:09:42] Selin Aydın: For the normal end I'd keep "Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum." for now. When the call routing project comes we look at all these sentences together anyway.
[00:09:50] Burcu Tan: Fine for me, as long as the failure one says "aktarıyorum".
[00:09:53] Deniz Arı: Noted. Failure after three tries: "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Normal end stays as it is in the document.
[00:10:01] Selin Aydın: Yes.
[00:10:03] Kerem Yalçın: Can someone close the door, there's a delivery guy shouting outside here.
[00:10:07] Burcu Tan: That's on your side Kerem [laughs].
[00:10:09] Kerem Yalçın: Ah, yes, sorry. One second. [inaudible]
[00:10:20] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Go on.
[00:10:22] Selin Aydın: Non-Turkish. Customer speaks English or Arabic or German, whatever.
[00:10:27] Deniz Arı: We assume this flow answers only in Turkish?
[00:10:30] Kerem Yalçın: Yes. For now only Turkish. There is an English menu in the IVR, they can go from the main menu.
[00:10:36] Ozan Er: So it doesn't answer the question, it just transfers. What does it say? Turkish, I assume, since the call is Turkish.
[00:10:42] Burcu Tan: Just "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." Nothing else. They won't understand a long sentence anyway.
[00:10:47] Selin Aydın: Okay. "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." for non-Turkish. Writing.
[00:10:52] Deniz Arı: Good.
[00:10:54] Selin Aydın: Out of scope next. So in the document I wrote out of scope goes directly to the main menu.

1	# A workflow shape that works for collection calls
2	
3	Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
4	outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
5	names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.
6	
7	## Contents
8	
9	1. The graph
10	2. Why it is shaped this way
11	3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
12	4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail
13	
14	## 1. The graph
15	
16	```text
17	setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
18	  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
19	       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
20	       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
21	            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
22	                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
23	                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record, note, close (ONE node, 3.9)
24	  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
25	       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
26	```
27	
28	Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
29	their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
30	graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.
31	
32	## 2. Why it is shaped this way
33	
34	- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
35	  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
36	  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
37	- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
38	  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
39	- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
40	  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
41	  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
42	  result means.
43	- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
44	  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
45	  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
46	- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
47	  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.
48	
49	## 3. Recipes
50	
51	All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
52	docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
53	code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.
54	
55	### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)
56	
57	Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.
58	
59	```python
60	src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
61	code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
62	node = {
63	  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
64	  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
65	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
66	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
67	          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
68	          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
69	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
70	}
71	```
72	
73	A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
74	are invented, take yours from the brief):
75	
76	```python
77	RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
78	             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
79	try:
80	    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
81	    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
82	    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
83	    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
84	except Exception as e:
85	    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
86	```
87	
88	What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
89	business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
90	band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
91	can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
92	and say which days it includes ("on or before").
93	
94	Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
95	negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
96	band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
97	product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
98	"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.
99	
100	**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
101	holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
102	the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
103	Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
104	per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:
105	
106	```python
107	def answer(d):
108	    parts = []
109	    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
110	        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
111	        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
112	        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
113	        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
114	    return "; ".join(parts)
115	vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
116	```
117	
118	The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
119	whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
120	prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
121	line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
122	named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.
123	
124	Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
125	--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
126	products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.
127	
128	### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
133	  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
134	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
135	    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
136	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
137	        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
138	        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
139	        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
140	        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
141	  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
142	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
143	}
144	```
145	
146	### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened
147	
148	Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
149	post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
150	means and the exact next thing to say or call.
151	
152	```python
153	POST = """try:
154	    if isinstance(result, dict):
155	        result.pop('header', None)
156	        d = result.get('data')
157	        if not isinstance(d, dict):
158	            d = dict()
159	            result['data'] = d
160	        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
161	        if ok:
162	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
163	        else:
164	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
165	except Exception:
166	    pass
167	"""
168	```
169	
170	**Treat "already exists" as success.** Write tools are not idempotent. Seen in a practice run:
171	the agent called the record tool, the customer said "okay" while the call was in flight, the new
172	turn called the same tool again, the bank answered "this product already has a promise", and the
173	hook reported a failure. The agent then told the customer it could not record a promise that was
174	recorded, and noted a service error. In every write tool's post-hook, read the API's error text:
175	when it says the record already exists, report it as RECORDED and tell the model not to call the
176	tool again for that item. Do not count it as a failed try.
177	
178	Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
179	`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
180	a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
181	and when to stop and close.
182	
183	Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
184	a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.
185	
186	### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node
187	
188	Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
189	the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
190	collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
191	in the field description.
192	
193	```json
194	"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
195	  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
196	  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
197	  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
198	```
199	
200	If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:
201	
202	```python
203	PRE = """try:
204	    b = config.get('body')
205	    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
206	        b.pop('reason', None)
207	except Exception:
208	    pass
209	"""
210	```
211	
212	Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:
213	
214	```json
215	{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
216	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
217	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
218	```
219	
220	```json
221	{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
222	 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
223	   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
224	```
225	
226	The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
227	for it). The end node hangs up silently.
228	
229	### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum
230	
231	Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
232	time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:
233	
234	```json
235	"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
236	  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
237	  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
238	"transitions": [
239	  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
240	  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
241	]
242	```
243	
244	Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
245	there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.
246	
247	A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
248	extract a different name there.
249	
250	### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines
251	
252	When the brief dictates what to say about the account (product names, amounts, days late, the
253	first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with
254	`on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}` in the negotiation node. The model then
255	cannot leave out a product, misread an amount or ask the wrong first question. Give the snippet a
256	fallback sentence for an empty product list.
257	
258	### 3.7 Name clashes with model-filled fields
259	
260	A tool field declared as `"default": "{{date}}"` is filled by the model only while no variable
261	`date` exists. If any node extracts or writes `date`, the field is baked from that value and the
262	model never sees it. Give extracted and code-written variables names that no tool field uses
263	(`wanted_date`, not `date`). The lint warns about this.
264	
265	### 3.8 Never enter a conversation node silently when the agent must act
266	
267	A conversation node with `on_enter: {"type": "silent"}` says nothing and WAITS FOR THE CUSTOMER.
268	Seen in a practice run: the call moved to a silent node after the customer's yes, both sides
269	waited, and every customer hung up. Silent is only for passthrough code and api_request nodes,
270	for the end node, and for a conversation node whose first move belongs to the customer. The lint
271	reports it as an error when such a node has a recording tool.
272	
273	### 3.9 Negotiate, read back, record and close in ONE node
274	
275	This is the design that passed every practice customer in four separate runs (plain speech,
276	answers in pieces, self-corrections, and three repetitions). Keep it.
277	
278	- One conversation node (`collect`) holds the negotiation AND the read-back AND the record tool,
279	  the note tool, the transfer tool and `close_call`. It is entered with a fixed `tts` line that
280	  states the debt (3.6).
281	- Do NOT split recording into a separate node. Tried twice, failed twice: a silent entry stalled
282	  the call, and an `llm` entry made one tool call and then stopped, leaving promises unrecorded
283	  and the call open.
284	- Enforce the order in the prompt with a numbered block the model cannot misread, placed before
285	  the negotiation rules, plus one worked example from the hardest case the brief describes:
286	
287	```text
288	STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
289	1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise
290	   or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it ended another way the brief names).
291	2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "<the brief's confirmation question>"
292	   and WAIT for the customer's answer.
293	3. Only after a clear yes: <record tool>, one per agreed product.
294	4. <note tool> for each product without a promise (only if the brief uses notes).
295	5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
296	NEVER call <record tool> in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do
297	step 2 and wait.
298	Example: <one customer turn that settles one product and refuses the others> = <what happens to
299	each product, attempt by attempt>; only then step 2.
300	```
301	
302	- The tool descriptions repeat the gate: record "CALL it only after the customer said a clear yes
303	  to the full read-back"; note "CALL it once per product without a recorded promise, after the
304	  promises are recorded".
305	- The post-hooks drive the sequence after the yes: a recorded promise says "call the record tool
306	  for the next agreed product now; when all are recorded say <the brief's sentence>; then notes;
307	  then close" (3.3).
308	- Persuasion attempts: "Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When
309	  its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer)". Do not add words such as
310	  REQUIRED: seen in a practice run, that made the agent make more attempts than the brief allows.
311	
312	`references/example_build.py` is that passing build script for the kit's practice brief. Read it
313	for the SHAPE: node graph, entry types, the hook helper, the order block, how facts reach the
314	prompt. Every sentence, value, outcome and rule in it belongs to that one brief. Never copy any
315	of them; write yours from your own spec.
316	
317	### 3.10 Answers given in pieces
318	
319	Final customers give numbers and dates in two parts ("forty four" ... "ten"), correct themselves,
320	and say them in words. Seen in a practice run: the agent asked for "all four digits" after each
321	part, five times, and never put "forty four" and "ten" together. In the identity prompt (and
322	wherever a number or date is collected):
323	- A partial answer is not wrong and not an answer: say "Yes?" or "And the rest?" and wait. Do not
324	  call the check tool on a part.
325	- Put the parts from consecutive turns together, in order, before calling the tool ("forty four",
326	  then "ten" is 4410; "nineteen October", then "nineteen eighty three" is 1983-10-19).
327	- When the customer corrects themselves ("the 21st, sorry, the 20th"), use the corrected value.
328	
329	## 4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail
330	
331	- **Sentences the brief dictates go in verbatim**, in quotes, in the node where they are said, and
332	  in the post-hook line of the tool after which they are said. The judge checks them word by word
333	  in spirit: a paraphrase of a required sentence often fails.
334	- **Words the brief forbids before a point** ("collections", "debt", a product) appear in a list
335	  in every prompt before that point. Do not write them anywhere else in those prompts, not even
336	  as examples.
337	- **Count limits in words the model can follow**: "You may make ONE persuasion attempt for this
338	  product. It is: <amount> on <date>." is better than "attempts depend on the band".
339	- **Give the agent the decision table, not the reasoning.** For each thing a customer can say
340	  (a date, a vague period, an amount, too much, a refusal, hardship, already paid, dispute, plan,
341	  human, scam, robot, wrong person), write the one response the brief requires, in brief order of
342	  priority. Say which rule wins when two apply.
343	- **Never ask what the brief forbids asking** (for example how much the customer can pay). Name
344	  the forbidden question in the prompt.
345	- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
346	- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
347	  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for
348	  example "To confirm: <product>, <amount>, on <date>. <confirmation question>". Seen in a practice
349	  run: the agent said "I have recorded a payment ... Do you confirm?" before any tool call, which
350	  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok
351	  ("recorded", "booked", "saved", "registered", "set up", "done").
352	- **Honesty**: say it is recorded only after a successful result, and never claim an action that
353	  was not a tool call. After a successful record, say plainly that it is recorded ("Your promise is
354	  recorded.") before any sentence the brief requires; after a failed try that succeeded on retry,
355	  this is how the customer learns it worked.
356	- **Attempts before giving up, per product**: a refusal does not end a product until the brief's
357	  persuasion attempts for that product are used. Seen in a practice run: the customer refused two
358	  of three products in one sentence and the agent noted both as refused at once, skipping the
359	  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer
360	  refuses: make attempt 1 as written in the account facts; if refused again and the product has
361	  attempt 2, make it; only then record the refusal (note, outcome)." When several products are
362	  refused together, go through them one at a time in the account order.
363	- **Keep prompts short.** Every rule in a prompt costs attention. Put rules where they apply, not
364	  in every node.
365

# A workflow shape that works for collection calls

Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.

## Contents

1. The graph
2. Why it is shaped this way
3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail

## 1. The graph

```text
setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record, note, close (ONE node, 3.9)
  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
```

Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.

## 2. Why it is shaped this way

- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
  result means.
- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.

## 3. Recipes

All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.

### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)

Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.

```python
src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
node = {
  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
}
```

A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
are invented, take yours from the brief):

```python
RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
try:
    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
except Exception as e:
    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
```

What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
and say which days it includes ("on or before").

Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.

**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:

```python
def answer(d):
    parts = []
    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
    return "; ".join(parts)
vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
```

The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.

Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.

### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
}
```

### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened

Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
means and the exact next thing to say or call.

```python
POST = """try:
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        result.pop('header', None)
        d = result.get('data')
        if not isinstance(d, dict):
            d = dict()
            result['data'] = d
        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
        if ok:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
        else:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

**Treat "already exists" as success.** Write tools are not idempotent. Seen in a practice run:
the agent called the record tool, the customer said "okay" while the call was in flight, the new
turn called the same tool again, the bank answered "this product already has a promise", and the
hook reported a failure. The agent then told the customer it could not record a promise that was
recorded, and noted a service error. In every write tool's post-hook, read the API's error text:
when it says the record already exists, report it as RECORDED and tell the model not to call the
tool again for that item. Do not count it as a failed try.

Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
and when to stop and close.

Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.

### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node

Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
in the field description.

```json
"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
```

If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:

```python
PRE = """try:
    b = config.get('body')
    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
        b.pop('reason', None)
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:

```json
{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
```

```json
{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
```

The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
for it). The end node hangs up silently.

### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum

Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:

```json
"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
"transitions": [
  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
]
```

Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.

A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
extract a different name there.

### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines

When the brief dictates what to say about the account (product names, amounts, days late, the
first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with
`on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}` in the negotiation node. The model then
cannot leave out a product, misread an amount or ask the wrong first question. Give the snippet a
fallback sentence for an empty product list.

### 3.7 Name clashes with model-filled fields

A tool field declared as `"default": "{{date}}"` is filled by the model only while no variable
`date` exists. If any node extracts or writes `date`, the field is baked from that value and the
model never sees it. Give extracted and code-written variables names that no tool field uses
(`wanted_date`, not `date`). The lint warns about this.

### 3.8 Never enter a conversation node silently when the agent must act

A conversation node with `on_enter: {"type": "silent"}` says nothing and WAITS FOR THE CUSTOMER.
Seen in a practice run: the call moved to a silent node after the customer's yes, both sides
waited, and every customer hung up. Silent is only for passthrough code and api_request nodes,
for the end node, and for a conversation node whose first move belongs to the customer. The lint
reports it as an error when such a node has a recording tool.

### 3.9 Negotiate, read back, record and close in ONE node

This is the design that passed every practice customer in four separate runs (plain speech,
answers in pieces, self-corrections, and three repetitions). Keep it.

- One conversation node (`collect`) holds the negotiation AND the read-back AND the record tool,
  the note tool, the transfer tool and `close_call`. It is entered with a fixed `tts` line that
  states the debt (3.6).
- Do NOT split recording into a separate node. Tried twice, failed twice: a silent entry stalled
  the call, and an `llm` entry made one tool call and then stopped, leaving promises unrecorded
  and the call open.
- Enforce the order in the prompt with a numbered block the model cannot misread, placed before
  the negotiation rules, plus one worked example from the hardest case the brief describes:

```text
STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise
   or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it ended another way the brief names).
2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "<the brief's confirmation question>"
   and WAIT for the customer's answer.
3. Only after a clear yes: <record tool>, one per agreed product.
4. <note tool> for each product without a promise (only if the brief uses notes).
5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
NEVER call <record tool> in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do
step 2 and wait.
Example: <one customer turn that settles one product and refuses the others> = <what happens to
each product, attempt by attempt>; only then step 2.
```

- The tool descriptions repeat the gate: record "CALL it only after the customer said a clear yes
  to the full read-back"; note "CALL it once per product without a recorded promise, after the
  promises are recorded".
- The post-hooks drive the sequence after the yes: a recorded promise says "call the record tool
  for the next agreed product now; when all are recorded say <the brief's sentence>; then notes;
  then close" (3.3).
- Persuasion attempts: "Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When
  its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer)". Do not add words such as
  REQUIRED: seen in a practice run, that made the agent make more attempts than the brief allows.

`references/example_build.py` is that passing build script for the kit's practice brief. Read it
for the SHAPE: node graph, entry types, the hook helper, the order block, how facts reach the
prompt. Every sentence, value, outcome and rule in it belongs to that one brief. Never copy any
of them; write yours from your own spec.

### 3.10 Answers given in pieces

Final customers give numbers and dates in two parts ("forty four" ... "ten"), correct themselves,
and say them in words. Seen in a practice run: the agent asked for "all four digits" after each
part, five times, and never put "forty four" and "ten" together. In the identity prompt (and
wherever a number or date is collected):
- A partial answer is not wrong and not an answer: say "Yes?" or "And the rest?" and wait. Do not
  call the check tool on a part.
- Put the parts from consecutive turns together, in order, before calling the tool ("forty four",
  then "ten" is 4410; "nineteen October", then "nineteen eighty three" is 1983-10-19).
- When the customer corrects themselves ("the 21st, sorry, the 20th"), use the corrected value.

## 4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail

- **Sentences the brief dictates go in verbatim**, in quotes, in the node where they are said, and
  in the post-hook line of the tool after which they are said. The judge checks them word by word
  in spirit: a paraphrase of a required sentence often fails.
- **Words the brief forbids before a point** ("collections", "debt", a product) appear in a list
  in every prompt before that point. Do not write them anywhere else in those prompts, not even
  as examples.
- **Count limits in words the model can follow**: "You may make ONE persuasion attempt for this
  product. It is: <amount> on <date>." is better than "attempts depend on the band".
- **Give the agent the decision table, not the reasoning.** For each thing a customer can say
  (a date, a vague period, an amount, too much, a refusal, hardship, already paid, dispute, plan,
  human, scam, robot, wrong person), write the one response the brief requires, in brief order of
  priority. Say which rule wins when two apply.
- **Never ask what the brief forbids asking** (for example how much the customer can pay). Name
  the forbidden question in the prompt.
- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for
  example "To confirm: <product>, <amount>, on <date>. <confirmation question>". Seen in a practice
  run: the agent said "I have recorded a payment ... Do you confirm?" before any tool call, which
  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok
  ("recorded", "booked", "saved", "registered", "set up", "done").
- **Honesty**: say it is recorded only after a successful result, and never claim an action that
  was not a tool call. After a successful record, say plainly that it is recorded ("Your promise is
  recorded.") before any sentence the brief requires; after a failed try that succeeded on retry,
  this is how the customer learns it worked.
- **Attempts before giving up, per product**: a refusal does not end a product until the brief's
  persuasion attempts for that product are used. Seen in a practice run: the customer refused two
  of three products in one sentence and the agent noted both as refused at once, skipping the
  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer
  refuses: make attempt 1 as written in the account facts; if refused again and the product has
  attempt 2, make it; only then record the refusal (note, outcome)." When several products are
  refused together, go through them one at a time in the account order.
- **Keep prompts short.** Every rule in a prompt costs attention. Put rules where they apply, not
  in every node.
