168	- If the day or time is outside the slots: ask ONCE for another time, naming the allowed window (today or the next business day, between 10:00 and 19:00). If the second answer is also outside, do not schedule: thank, goodbye, close_call not_reached / no_callback. Also no_callback if they give no time.
169	- If they say the number does not belong to the customer: close_call not_reached / wrong_number.
170	- If they say the customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, goodbye, close_call not_reached / deceased."""
171	
172	IDENTITY_TASK = FORBID + """
173	The customer confirmed who they are. Check identity with two security questions, one at a time.
174	1. Say that for security you need to ask two questions, and ask for their date of birth. When they answer, call verify_identity with field date_of_birth and answer as YYYY-MM-DD. A date given only as numbers is day, then month, then year (03/06/1987 = 1987-06-03). Convert spoken dates yourself.
175	2. Then ask for the last four digits of the phone number on file and call verify_identity with field phone_last4 and the four digits.
176	Follow what_to_do_next after each result. Never reveal what is on file.
177	- Customers often give an answer in PIECES over several turns ("nineteen October" then "nineteen eighty three"; "forty four" then "ten" = 4410). Combine the pieces of the current answer. If the answer is not complete yet, reply only "Yes, go on." (do NOT repeat the question). As soon as you have a full date or four digits, call verify_identity.
178	- If they do not want to answer, or ask what the call is about instead of answering: explain ONCE that the questions protect their account and ask again. If they refuse again or ask again: thank, goodbye, close_call not_verified / declined.
179	- A request for a human follows the system rule (transfer queue general, close transferred / human)."""
180	
181	COLLECT_TASK = """Identity is verified. You have already said this aloud: "{{debt_statement}}"
182	
183	ACCOUNT FACTS (one line per product, in order):
184	{{account_facts}}
185	
186	{{date_facts}}
187	DATE ANSWERS: when the customer names a day, find it here and do exactly what its line says for each product:
188	{{date_answers}}
189	
190	STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
191	1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it is paid/dispute/hardship).
192	2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "Do you confirm?" and WAIT for the customer's answer.
193	3. Only after a clear yes: create_promise, one per agreed product.
194	4. add_note for each product without a promise.
195	5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
196	NEVER call create_promise in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do step 2 and wait.
197	Example: "I'll pay the card tomorrow, not the other two" = card agreed for tomorrow (check DATE ANSWERS); then the second product: make its attempt 1; if refused and it has attempt 2, make attempt 2; then the third product the same way; only then step 2.
198	
199	HOW TO NEGOTIATE
200	- The question about paying today is asked ONCE for all products (already asked). If yes for all: the promise is the full amount of every product dated today.
201	- If not all today: go through the products one by one in the order above. For each product start at its attempt 1. Never ask about today again.
202	- Always ask for the full past-due amount first. NEVER ask "how much can you pay?" - you propose every amount.
203	- Customer names a date: use DATE ANSWERS. A vague period ("next week", "end of month", "when my salary comes"): ask once for the exact day; a named day then goes through DATE ANSWERS; if still none, propose that product's deadline.
204	- "Next <weekday>" = that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" = in the current week.
205	- If the customer names ONE date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, that product gets its own deadline and the others keep the named date; say so in the read-back.
206	- Full amount too much: offer the product's floor once and say the rest stays overdue. Amount from floor to full (inclusive): accept. Below floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
207	- A proposed date or amount is never a refusal.
208	- Flat refusal, non-answer, refusing the floor, refusing the deadline offer: that uses one persuasion attempt for that product. Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer): that product is refused. When several products are refused in one sentence, still go through them one at a time with their attempts.
209	- Illness, death in the family or job loss: one short sentence of sympathy, NO persuasion; offer to connect them with the customer support team. Accept: transfer_to_agent queue support, close transferred / support. Decline: the remaining unpromised products get note hardship. If they still name a date or amount themselves, handle it normally.
210	- "I already paid" (this past-due amount) for a product: say payments can take one business day to appear; no promise for it; it gets note paid; continue with the other products.
211	- "Not mine" / "never had it" / "closed or paid off in the past": do not argue; no promise; note dispute; continue with the others.
212	- New payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Do NOT record any agreed-but-unrecorded promise. Call transfer_to_agent queue restructuring, close transferred / restructuring.
213	- On ANY transfer never call add_note, before or after it.
214	- Customer says twice they do not want to talk: remaining products get note refused, then close.
215	- Recorded promises cannot be changed or cancelled; they can change it in the mobile app.
216	
217	READ-BACK AND RECORDING
218	- When every product is settled (promise agreed or no promise), read ALL agreed promises back together in ONE message in future tense: "To confirm: <product> <amount> on <weekday day month>; <next product> ... Do you confirm?" Do not use the words recorded, booked, saved, registered, set up or done before create_promise returned ok.
219	- If they change a date or amount, check it again and read everything back again.
220	- After a clear yes: call create_promise once per agreed product (product_id, amount as a number, date YYYY-MM-DD), one at a time, in order. Follow what_to_do_next.
221	- Then for EACH product without a recorded promise call add_note with its product_id and reason (refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error). Also when no product has a promise.
222	
223	CLOSING (thank and say goodbye in the same turn as close_call)
224	- At least one promise recorded and no transfer: outcome promise.
225	- Transfer happened: outcome transferred with that transfer's reason.
226	- No promise recorded: if every product is noted paid, outcome paid; otherwise outcome no_promise with the reason of the FIRST product in account order whose note is not paid."""
227	
228	WF = {
229	    "initial_node": "setup",
230	    "system_prompt": SYSTEM,
231	    "test_variables": {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Dana", "last_name": "Fisher", "title": "Ms", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"},
232	    "nodes": {},
233	}
234	N = WF["nodes"]
235	N["setup"] = code_node("setup", SETUP_CODE, "greet")
236	
237	N["greet"] = {
238	    "name": "greet", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": OPENING}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
239	    "task_message": GREET_TASK,
240	    "extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
241	                           "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "wrong_number", "unclear"],
242	                           "description": "Who answered. customer ONLY if the person said yes, that's me, speaking, or the customer's own name. someone_else if the person says they are someone else (a relative, colleague, etc.) or the customer is not available. wrong_number if the number does not belong to the customer. Otherwise unclear (hello, go ahead, who is this, questions)."}],
243	    "tools": [close_tool(["not_reached", "not_verified", "transferred"], ["unclear", "wrong_number", "deceased", "declined", "human"],
244	                         "not_reached/unclear: still unclear after the second ask. not_reached/wrong_number: not the customer's number. not_reached/deceased: customer has died. not_verified/declined: refuses to talk twice. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
245	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
246	    "transitions": [END_T,
247	                    {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
248	                    {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}],
249	}
250	
251	N["third_party"] = {
252	    "name": "third_party", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
253	    "task_message": THIRD_TASK,
254	    "tools": [api_tool("schedule_callback", "Book a callback. CALL it only when the person gave a day and time inside the allowed callback slots.",
255	                       {"date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_date}}", "description": "Callback date YYYY-MM-DD, today or the next business day only."},
256	                        "time": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_time}}", "description": "Callback time HH:MM, 24h, from 10:00 to 19:00."}},
257	                       ["date", "time"], retries=0, post=CALLBACK_POST),
258	              close_tool(["not_reached", "transferred"], ["callback", "no_callback", "wrong_number", "deceased", "human"],
259	                         "not_reached/callback: callback booked. not_reached/no_callback: no valid time after one re-ask. not_reached/wrong_number. not_reached/deceased. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
260	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
261	    "transitions": [END_T],
262	}
263	
264	N["identity"] = {
265	    "name": "identity", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
266	    "task_message": IDENTITY_TASK,
267	    "tools": [api_tool("verify_identity", "Check one security answer. CALL it every time the customer answers a security question.",
268	                       {"field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["date_of_birth", "phone_last4"], "default": "{{field}}", "description": "date_of_birth for the first question, phone_last4 for the second."},
269	                        "answer": {"type": "string", "default": "{{answer}}", "description": "date_of_birth as YYYY-MM-DD (numbers only: day, month, year); phone_last4 as four digits."}},
270	                       ["field", "answer"], retries=1, post=VERIFY_POST),
271	              close_tool(["not_verified", "transferred"], ["failed", "declined", "human"],
272	                         "not_verified/failed: three wrong answers. not_verified/declined: refused the questions twice (or asked what the call is about twice). transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
273	              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the customer insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
274	    "transitions": [END_T,
275	                    {"target_node": "fetch_account", "description": "identity verified", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
276	                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
277	                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}],
278	}
279	
280	fetch = api_tool("get_account", "Get the late products.", {}, [], retries=2)
281	N["fetch_account"] = {"name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": "account",
282	                      "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "pre_actions": [fetch],
283	                      "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
284	                      "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]}
285	N["account"] = code_node("account", ACCOUNT_CODE, "collect")
286	
287	N["collect"] = {
288	    "name": "collect", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
289	    "task_message": COLLECT_TASK,
290	    "tools": [api_tool("create_promise", "Record one payment promise for one product. CALL it only after the customer said a clear yes to the full read-back, once per agreed product.",
291	                       {"product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "product_id from the account facts"},
292	                        "amount": {"type": "number", "default": "{{amount}}", "description": "Agreed amount, a number, from the floor up to the full past-due amount."},
293	                        "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "Agreed date YYYY-MM-DD, a business day, today or later, not after the product's deadline."}},
294	                       ["product_id", "amount", "date"], retries=0, post=PROMISE_POST),
295	              api_tool("add_note", "Record why one product ended without a promise. CALL it once per product without a recorded promise, after the promises are recorded. NEVER call it when a transfer happened or will happen.",
296	                       {"product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "product_id from the account facts"},
297	                        "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["refused", "hardship", "dispute", "paid", "service_error"], "default": "{{note_reason}}", "description": "refused: attempts used up or refuses to talk; hardship: hardship and declined support; dispute: not mine / never had it / closed; paid: already paid this amount; service_error: create_promise failed twice."}},
298	                       ["product_id", "reason"], retries=0, post=NOTE_POST),
299	              transfer_tool(["restructuring", "general", "support"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it for a new payment plan or lower instalments (restructuring), a customer who insists on a human after one offer of help (general), or hardship when the customer accepts support (support)."),
300	              close_tool(["promise", "paid", "transferred", "no_promise"], ["refused", "hardship", "dispute", "service_error", "restructuring", "human", "support"],
301	                         "promise: at least one promise recorded (no transfer). paid: no promise and every product noted paid. transferred + restructuring/human/support: after a transfer. no_promise + the reason of the first product (account order) whose note is not paid.")],
302	    "transitions": [END_T],
303	}
304	
305	N["end"] = {"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "transitions": [],
306	            "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
307	                         "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
308	
309	with open("out/brief-b.workflow.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
310	    json.dump(WF, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
311	print("written")

# EXAMPLE ONLY: the build script that passed every practice customer of the kit's Brief A + B
# (4 separate runs: plain speech, answers in pieces, self-corrections, 3 repetitions).
#
# Use it for the SHAPE: the node graph (setup -> greet -> third_party | identity -> fetch_account
# -> account -> collect -> end), entry types, the hook() helper, the per-node close_call enums,
# and the STRICT ORDER block in COLLECT_TASK. Recording happens in collect itself.
#
# Every sentence, value, word list, outcome, reason and rule below belongs to that one brief.
# Do NOT copy any of it into another brief's agent. Write yours from your own spec.
#

import json, subprocess, sys, os

SKILL = ".claude/skills/build-phone-agent"
SERVER = "https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev/v1"


def code_of(snippet, out):
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", snippet, "--out", out], check=True)
    return open(out, encoding="utf-8").read()


SETUP_CODE = code_of("out/brief-b_setup_snippet.py", "out/brief-b_setup_code.txt")
ACCOUNT_CODE = code_of("out/brief-b_account_snippet.py", "out/brief-b_account_code.txt")


def code_node(name, code, target):
    return {"name": name, "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": target,
            "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
            "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
                    "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
            "transitions": [{"target_node": target, "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]}


def api_tool(name, desc, body_props, required, retries=0, post="", pre="", timeout=12000):
    props = {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}", "description": "The customer id."}}
    props.update(body_props)
    t = {"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": timeout, "maxRetries": retries},
         "function": {"name": name, "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": desc,
                      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                          "url": {"type": "string", "default": SERVER + "/" + name},
                          "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
                          "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
                          "body": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required}}}}}
    if post:
        t["post_process_code"] = post
    if pre:
        t["pre_process_code"] = pre
    return t


def hook(body):
    lines = ["try:", "    if isinstance(result, dict):", "        result.pop('header', None)",
             "        d = result.get('data')", "        if not isinstance(d, dict):", "            d = dict()",
             "            result['data'] = d",
             "        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400",
             "        err = str(d.get('error') or result.get('message') or '').lower()"]
    lines += ["        " + l for l in body.strip("\n").split("\n")]
    lines += ["except Exception:", "    pass", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


VERIFY_POST = hook("""
left = d.get('wrong_answers_left')
if d.get('all_verified') is True or str(d.get('all_verified')) in ('true', 'True'):
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'IDENTITY VERIFIED. Say only: Thank you, that is confirmed. Nothing else.'
elif d.get('hint') == 'day_month_swapped':
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Not counted as wrong. Ask the customer to say their date of birth again with the month as a word, for example the 3rd of June 1987.'
elif not ok and d.get('verified') is None:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The answer could not be read and was NOT counted. Ask the same question again; for a date ask for day, month as a word, and year.'
elif d.get('verified') is True:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Correct. Now ask the second question: the last four digits of the phone number on file.'
elif left is not None and int(left) <= 0:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'CHECK FAILED, no tries left. Do not mention any account, amount or reason for the call. Say they can use the Freya Bank mobile app or visit a branch, thank them, say goodbye, and call close_call with outcome not_verified and reason failed.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Wrong answer. Ask the SAME question once more, without saying what is on file.'
""")

PROMISE_POST = hook("""
if ok or 'already' in err or 'exists' in err:
    d['ok'] = True
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED for this product_id. Never call create_promise again for this product. If another agreed promise from the read-back is not recorded yet, call create_promise for it now. When all are recorded, say exactly: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." Then, for any product without a promise, call add_note; then close.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. If this was the FIRST try for this product, call create_promise again now with exactly the same values. If it was the SECOND failed try, say you could not record the promise for this product, call add_note for it with reason service_error, then continue with the other products.'
""")

NOTE_POST = hook("""
if ok or 'already' in err or 'exists' in err:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Note saved. Never note this product again. Continue with the next product in order; if every product is handled, give the closing words and call close_call per the closing rule.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The note failed. Call add_note once more with the same values.'
""")

TRANSFER_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'TRANSFERRED. Do NOT call add_note or create_promise. Say thank you and goodbye, then call close_call with outcome transferred and reason restructuring (queue restructuring), human (queue general) or support (queue support).'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The transfer failed. Call transfer_to_agent once more with the same queue.'
""")

CALLBACK_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Callback booked. Thank them, say goodbye, call close_call with outcome not_reached and reason callback.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT booked. Call schedule_callback once more with the same values. If it fails again, say it could not be booked, thank them and close with not_reached and reason no_callback.'
""")

CLOSE_POST = hook("""
if ok:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'The call is closed. Say nothing more.'
else:
    d['what_to_do_next'] = 'close_call failed. Call close_call once more with the same values.'
""")

CLOSE_PRE = """try:
    b = config.get('body')
    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('promise', 'paid'):
        b.pop('reason', None)
except Exception:
    pass
"""


def close_tool(outcomes, reasons, desc):
    props = {"outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": outcomes, "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": desc},
             "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": reasons, "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "The reason that goes with the outcome. Leave empty for promise and paid."}}
    return api_tool("close_call", "End the call. CALL it exactly once, as the very last tool call, in the same turn as your thank-you and goodbye. " + desc,
                    props, ["outcome"], retries=0, post=CLOSE_POST, pre=CLOSE_PRE)


def transfer_tool(queues, desc):
    return api_tool("transfer_to_agent", desc, {"queue": {"type": "string", "enum": queues, "default": "{{queue}}", "description": "restructuring = new payment plan or lower instalments; general = the customer insists on a human; support = hardship and accepted support."}},
                    ["queue"], retries=0, post=TRANSFER_POST)


END_T = {"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
    {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
    {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}

FORBID = 'Before identity is verified NEVER say any of these words or hint at them: "collections", "debt", "payment", "owe", "late", "overdue", "account", "loan", "credit card", "product". If asked what the call is about, say only that it is a personal matter for {{title}} {{last_name}}.'

SYSTEM = """You are Freya Bank's digital assistant on an outbound phone call. Speak English. Be brief and polite: one or two short sentences per turn, ONE question per turn.
After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end a turn with nothing said. Call one tool at a time.
Address the customer as {{title}} {{last_name}}.
If asked whether you are a robot or an AI: say you are Freya Bank's digital assistant, then continue with your current question.
If asked whether this is a scam: say they can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, then continue with your current question.
If the person asks for a human: the first time ask whether you can help them first. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent with queue general, then close as transferred with reason human.
A question you cannot answer from your facts or tools: say you do not have that information. Never invent figures, dates or reasons.
Never claim an action happened unless its tool returned ok. Never offer a discount, waiver, instalment plan or any other term.
Before close_call always thank the customer and say goodbye, in the same turn as the close_call call. close_call is always the last tool call."""

OPENING = "Hello, this is Freya Bank's digital assistant calling. This call is recorded. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?"

GREET_TASK = FORBID + """
You asked whether you are speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}. No tool call except close_call and transfer_to_agent is allowed here.
- Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead", "who is this" do NOT.
- If it is not a confirmation (or they asked a question; answer it first per the rules), ask again exactly: "Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?" This is your second and last ask. If still unclear after the second ask: thank them, say goodbye, call close_call with outcome not_reached, reason unclear.
- If they say this number does not belong to that person: apologise, say goodbye, close_call not_reached / wrong_number.
- If they say the customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." Ask nothing else, say goodbye, close_call not_reached / deceased.
- If the person refuses to talk twice: thank them, goodbye, close_call not_verified / declined."""

THIRD_TASK = FORBID + """
Someone other than {{title}} {{last_name}} is on the line. Do not say why you are calling. Do not answer any question about the customer or any money matter, even if they offer to pay; say only that it is a personal matter. Ask when {{title}} {{last_name}} can be reached.
{{callback_facts}}
- If they name a day and time inside the allowed slots: call schedule_callback with date YYYY-MM-DD and time HH:MM (24h). Then thank, goodbye, close_call not_reached / callback.
- If the day or time is outside the slots: ask ONCE for another time, naming the allowed window (today or the next business day, between 10:00 and 19:00). If the second answer is also outside, do not schedule: thank, goodbye, close_call not_reached / no_callback. Also no_callback if they give no time.
- If they say the number does not belong to the customer: close_call not_reached / wrong_number.
- If they say the customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, goodbye, close_call not_reached / deceased."""

IDENTITY_TASK = FORBID + """
The customer confirmed who they are. Check identity with two security questions, one at a time.
1. Say that for security you need to ask two questions, and ask for their date of birth. When they answer, call verify_identity with field date_of_birth and answer as YYYY-MM-DD. A date given only as numbers is day, then month, then year (03/06/1987 = 1987-06-03). Convert spoken dates yourself.
2. Then ask for the last four digits of the phone number on file and call verify_identity with field phone_last4 and the four digits.
Follow what_to_do_next after each result. Never reveal what is on file.
- Customers often give an answer in PIECES over several turns ("nineteen October" then "nineteen eighty three"; "forty four" then "ten" = 4410). Combine the pieces of the current answer. If the answer is not complete yet, reply only "Yes, go on." (do NOT repeat the question). As soon as you have a full date or four digits, call verify_identity.
- If they do not want to answer, or ask what the call is about instead of answering: explain ONCE that the questions protect their account and ask again. If they refuse again or ask again: thank, goodbye, close_call not_verified / declined.
- A request for a human follows the system rule (transfer queue general, close transferred / human)."""

COLLECT_TASK = """Identity is verified. You have already said this aloud: "{{debt_statement}}"

ACCOUNT FACTS (one line per product, in order):
{{account_facts}}

{{date_facts}}
DATE ANSWERS: when the customer names a day, find it here and do exactly what its line says for each product:
{{date_answers}}

STRICT ORDER OF THE CALL (never skip a step):
1. Negotiate every product, one at a time, in account order, until each has an agreed promise or its persuasion attempts are all used (or it is paid/dispute/hardship).
2. Read ALL agreed promises back in ONE message ending with "Do you confirm?" and WAIT for the customer's answer.
3. Only after a clear yes: create_promise, one per agreed product.
4. add_note for each product without a promise.
5. Thank, say goodbye, and call close_call in that same message.
NEVER call create_promise in the turn where the customer agrees to a date or amount: first do step 2 and wait.
Example: "I'll pay the card tomorrow, not the other two" = card agreed for tomorrow (check DATE ANSWERS); then the second product: make its attempt 1; if refused and it has attempt 2, make attempt 2; then the third product the same way; only then step 2.

HOW TO NEGOTIATE
- The question about paying today is asked ONCE for all products (already asked). If yes for all: the promise is the full amount of every product dated today.
- If not all today: go through the products one by one in the order above. For each product start at its attempt 1. Never ask about today again.
- Always ask for the full past-due amount first. NEVER ask "how much can you pay?" - you propose every amount.
- Customer names a date: use DATE ANSWERS. A vague period ("next week", "end of month", "when my salary comes"): ask once for the exact day; a named day then goes through DATE ANSWERS; if still none, propose that product's deadline.
- "Next <weekday>" = that weekday in the following calendar week; "this <weekday>" = in the current week.
- If the customer names ONE date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, that product gets its own deadline and the others keep the named date; say so in the read-back.
- Full amount too much: offer the product's floor once and say the rest stays overdue. Amount from floor to full (inclusive): accept. Below floor: say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once.
- A proposed date or amount is never a refusal.
- Flat refusal, non-answer, refusing the floor, refusing the deadline offer: that uses one persuasion attempt for that product. Make the product's next attempt exactly as written in ACCOUNT FACTS. When its attempts are used up, stop (never repeat a refused offer): that product is refused. When several products are refused in one sentence, still go through them one at a time with their attempts.
- Illness, death in the family or job loss: one short sentence of sympathy, NO persuasion; offer to connect them with the customer support team. Accept: transfer_to_agent queue support, close transferred / support. Decline: the remaining unpromised products get note hardship. If they still name a date or amount themselves, handle it normally.
- "I already paid" (this past-due amount) for a product: say payments can take one business day to appear; no promise for it; it gets note paid; continue with the other products.
- "Not mine" / "never had it" / "closed or paid off in the past": do not argue; no promise; note dispute; continue with the others.
- New payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Do NOT record any agreed-but-unrecorded promise. Call transfer_to_agent queue restructuring, close transferred / restructuring.
- On ANY transfer never call add_note, before or after it.
- Customer says twice they do not want to talk: remaining products get note refused, then close.
- Recorded promises cannot be changed or cancelled; they can change it in the mobile app.

READ-BACK AND RECORDING
- When every product is settled (promise agreed or no promise), read ALL agreed promises back together in ONE message in future tense: "To confirm: <product> <amount> on <weekday day month>; <next product> ... Do you confirm?" Do not use the words recorded, booked, saved, registered, set up or done before create_promise returned ok.
- If they change a date or amount, check it again and read everything back again.
- After a clear yes: call create_promise once per agreed product (product_id, amount as a number, date YYYY-MM-DD), one at a time, in order. Follow what_to_do_next.
- Then for EACH product without a recorded promise call add_note with its product_id and reason (refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error). Also when no product has a promise.

CLOSING (thank and say goodbye in the same turn as close_call)
- At least one promise recorded and no transfer: outcome promise.
- Transfer happened: outcome transferred with that transfer's reason.
- No promise recorded: if every product is noted paid, outcome paid; otherwise outcome no_promise with the reason of the FIRST product in account order whose note is not paid."""

WF = {
    "initial_node": "setup",
    "system_prompt": SYSTEM,
    "test_variables": {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Dana", "last_name": "Fisher", "title": "Ms", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"},
    "nodes": {},
}
N = WF["nodes"]
N["setup"] = code_node("setup", SETUP_CODE, "greet")

N["greet"] = {
    "name": "greet", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": OPENING}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
    "task_message": GREET_TASK,
    "extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
                           "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "wrong_number", "unclear"],
                           "description": "Who answered. customer ONLY if the person said yes, that's me, speaking, or the customer's own name. someone_else if the person says they are someone else (a relative, colleague, etc.) or the customer is not available. wrong_number if the number does not belong to the customer. Otherwise unclear (hello, go ahead, who is this, questions)."}],
    "tools": [close_tool(["not_reached", "not_verified", "transferred"], ["unclear", "wrong_number", "deceased", "declined", "human"],
                         "not_reached/unclear: still unclear after the second ask. not_reached/wrong_number: not the customer's number. not_reached/deceased: customer has died. not_verified/declined: refuses to talk twice. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
    "transitions": [END_T,
                    {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
                    {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}],
}

N["third_party"] = {
    "name": "third_party", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
    "task_message": THIRD_TASK,
    "tools": [api_tool("schedule_callback", "Book a callback. CALL it only when the person gave a day and time inside the allowed callback slots.",
                       {"date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_date}}", "description": "Callback date YYYY-MM-DD, today or the next business day only."},
                        "time": {"type": "string", "default": "{{cb_time}}", "description": "Callback time HH:MM, 24h, from 10:00 to 19:00."}},
                       ["date", "time"], retries=0, post=CALLBACK_POST),
              close_tool(["not_reached", "transferred"], ["callback", "no_callback", "wrong_number", "deceased", "human"],
                         "not_reached/callback: callback booked. not_reached/no_callback: no valid time after one re-ask. not_reached/wrong_number. not_reached/deceased. transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the person insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
    "transitions": [END_T],
}

N["identity"] = {
    "name": "identity", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "llm"},
    "task_message": IDENTITY_TASK,
    "tools": [api_tool("verify_identity", "Check one security answer. CALL it every time the customer answers a security question.",
                       {"field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["date_of_birth", "phone_last4"], "default": "{{field}}", "description": "date_of_birth for the first question, phone_last4 for the second."},
                        "answer": {"type": "string", "default": "{{answer}}", "description": "date_of_birth as YYYY-MM-DD (numbers only: day, month, year); phone_last4 as four digits."}},
                       ["field", "answer"], retries=1, post=VERIFY_POST),
              close_tool(["not_verified", "transferred"], ["failed", "declined", "human"],
                         "not_verified/failed: three wrong answers. not_verified/declined: refused the questions twice (or asked what the call is about twice). transferred/human: after transfer_to_agent general."),
              transfer_tool(["general"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it only when the customer insists on a human after you asked once whether you can help.")],
    "transitions": [END_T,
                    {"target_node": "fetch_account", "description": "identity verified", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
                        {"variable": "verify_identity_response.data.all_verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}],
}

fetch = api_tool("get_account", "Get the late products.", {}, [], retries=2)
N["fetch_account"] = {"name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": "account",
                      "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "pre_actions": [fetch],
                      "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
                      "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]}
N["account"] = code_node("account", ACCOUNT_CODE, "collect")

N["collect"] = {
    "name": "collect", "node_type": "conversation", "on_enter": {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}, "on_enter_first_entry_only": True,
    "task_message": COLLECT_TASK,
    "tools": [api_tool("create_promise", "Record one payment promise for one product. CALL it only after the customer said a clear yes to the full read-back, once per agreed product.",
                       {"product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "product_id from the account facts"},
                        "amount": {"type": "number", "default": "{{amount}}", "description": "Agreed amount, a number, from the floor up to the full past-due amount."},
                        "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "Agreed date YYYY-MM-DD, a business day, today or later, not after the product's deadline."}},
                       ["product_id", "amount", "date"], retries=0, post=PROMISE_POST),
              api_tool("add_note", "Record why one product ended without a promise. CALL it once per product without a recorded promise, after the promises are recorded. NEVER call it when a transfer happened or will happen.",
                       {"product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}", "description": "product_id from the account facts"},
                        "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["refused", "hardship", "dispute", "paid", "service_error"], "default": "{{note_reason}}", "description": "refused: attempts used up or refuses to talk; hardship: hardship and declined support; dispute: not mine / never had it / closed; paid: already paid this amount; service_error: create_promise failed twice."}},
                       ["product_id", "reason"], retries=0, post=NOTE_POST),
              transfer_tool(["restructuring", "general", "support"], "Hand the call to a person. CALL it for a new payment plan or lower instalments (restructuring), a customer who insists on a human after one offer of help (general), or hardship when the customer accepts support (support)."),
              close_tool(["promise", "paid", "transferred", "no_promise"], ["refused", "hardship", "dispute", "service_error", "restructuring", "human", "support"],
                         "promise: at least one promise recorded (no transfer). paid: no promise and every product noted paid. transferred + restructuring/human/support: after a transfer. no_promise + the reason of the first product (account order) whose note is not paid.")],
    "transitions": [END_T],
}

N["end"] = {"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "transitions": [],
            "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
                         "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}

1	# Tools and code
2	
3	This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.
4	
5	Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.
6	
7	## Tool function shape
8	
9	Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "type": "function",
14	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
15	  "function": {
16	    "name": "lookup_order",
17	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
18	    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
19	    "parameters": {
20	      "type": "object",
21	      "properties": {
22	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
23	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
24	        "headers": {
25	          "type": "object",
26	          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
27	        },
28	        "body": {
29	          "type": "object",
30	          "properties": {
31	            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
32	            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
33	          },
34	          "required": ["order_number"]
35	        }
36	      }
37	    }
38	  },
39	  "response_mapping": [
40	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
41	  ]
42	}
43	```
44	
45	| Field | Meaning |
46	|---|---|
47	| `type` | Always `"function"` |
48	| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
49	| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
50	| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
51	| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
52	| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
53	| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
54	| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
55	| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
56	| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
57	| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
58	| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |
59	
60	| Handler | Runs |
61	|---|---|
62	| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
63	| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
64	| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |
65	
66	Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.
67	
68	`api_call` parameters:
69	
70	| Parameter | Meaning |
71	|---|---|
72	| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
73	| `method` | HTTP method |
74	| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
75	| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
76	| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |
77	
78	## How a parameter gets its value
79	
80	One key decides, per parameter: `default`.
81	
82	| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
85	| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
86	| no `default` | The model | Yes |
87	| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |
88	
89	Rules:
90	
91	- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
92	- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
93	- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.
94	
95	The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.
96	
97	Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.
98	
99	Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.
100	
101	### `api_call` body field rules
102	
103	- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
104	- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
105	- Give each leaf its own `default`.
106	- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
107	- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.
108	
109	A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.
110	
111	### When a baked variable has no value
112	
113	| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
116	| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |
117	
118	Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.
119	
120	### Constrain model-filled parameters
121	
122	When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.
123	
124	- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
125	- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
126	- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.
127	
128	```json
129	{
130	  "type": "object",
131	  "properties": {
132	    "queue": {
133	      "type": "string",
134	      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
135	      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
136	      "default": "{{queue}}"
137	    }
138	  },
139	  "required": ["queue"]
140	}
141	```
142	
143	## `pre_actions` versus `tools`
144	
145	The placement decides who fires the call.
146	
147	| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
150	| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
151	| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |
152	
153	The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.
154	
155	**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.
156	
157	**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.
158	
159	Differences in behaviour:
160	
161	| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
164	| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
165	| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
166	| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
167	| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |
168	
169	To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.
170	
171	### A `pre_actions` node
172	
173	```json
174	{
175	  "name": "fetch_order",
176	  "node_type": "api_request",
177	  "passthrough": true,
178	  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
179	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
180	  "pre_actions": [
181	    {
182	      "type": "function",
183	      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
184	      "function": {
185	        "name": "get_order",
186	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
187	        "description": "Get the order.",
188	        "parameters": {
189	          "type": "object",
190	          "properties": {
191	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
192	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
193	            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
194	            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
195	          }
196	        }
197	      }
198	    }
199	  ],
200	  "response_mapping": [
201	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
202	  ],
203	  "transitions": [
204	    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
205	  ]
206	}
207	```
208	
209	The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.
210	
211	### Tool descriptions
212	
213	In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.
214	
215	- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
216	- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
217	- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
218	- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
219	- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".
220	
221	A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."
222	
223	## `response_mapping`
224	
225	`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.
226	
227	```json
228	{
229	  "response_mapping": [
230	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
231	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
232	  ]
233	}
234	```
235	
236	| Field | Meaning |
237	|---|---|
238	| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
239	| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |
240	
241	### Placement
242	
243	- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
244	- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.
245	
246	`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.
247	
248	### Where a result lands (trial findings)
249	
250	Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.
251	
252	```json
253	{
254	  "status": "success",
255	  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
256	  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
257	  "status_code": 200,
258	  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
259	}
260	```
261	
262	`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.
263	
264	The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:
265	
266	| Variable | Value |
267	|---|---|
268	| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
269	| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
270	| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
271	| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
272	| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
273	| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
274	| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
275	| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
276	| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
277	| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |
278	
279	Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.
280	
281	### Which mapping paths work
282	
283	- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
284	- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
285	- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
286	- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
287	- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.
288	
289	## Routing on tool results
290	
291	Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.
292	
293	```json
294	{
295	  "transitions": [
296	    {
297	      "target_node": "load_order",
298	      "description": "The check passed",
299	      "condition": {
300	        "logic": "or",
301	        "conditions": [
302	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
303	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
304	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
305	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
306	        ]
307	      }
308	    }
309	  ]
310	}
311	```
312	
313	Rules:
314	
315	- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
316	- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
317	- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.
318	
319	### Success and failure counters
320	
321	The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.
322	
323	| Placement | Variables |
324	|---|---|
325	| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
326	| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |
327	
328	Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "transitions": [
333	    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
334	    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
335	  ]
336	}
337	```
338	
339	### `suppress_tool_results`
340	
341	A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.
342	
343	### Background tools
344	
345	A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.
346	
347	## Retries and timeouts
348	
349	| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
350	|---|---|---|---|
351	| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
352	| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
353	| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
354	| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |
355	
356	`connect_retries` in detail:
357	
358	- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
359	- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
360	- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
361	- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
362	- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
363	- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.
364	
365	The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.
366	
367	## Pre and post Python hooks
368	
369	An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.
370	
371	```json
372	{
373	  "type": "function",
374	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
375	  "function": {
376	    "name": "check_answer",
377	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
378	    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
379	    "parameters": {
380	      "type": "object",
381	      "properties": {
382	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
383	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
384	        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
385	      }
386	    }
387	  },
388	  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
389	  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
390	}
391	```
392	
393	| Hook | Names available | Use |
394	|---|---|---|
395	| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
396	| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |
397	
398	Documented behaviour:
399	
400	- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
401	- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
402	- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
403	- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.
404	
405	### What `result` looks like in a post-hook
406	
407	The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:
408	
409	- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
410	- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
411	- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
412	- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.
413	
414	The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.
415	
416	Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.
417	
418	## Code nodes and `code_exec`
419	
420	A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.
421	
422	```json
423	{
424	  "name": "compute_delivery",
425	  "node_type": "code",
426	  "passthrough": true,
427	  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
428	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
429	  "pre_actions": [
430	    {
431	      "type": "function",
432	      "function": {
433	        "name": "code_exec",
434	        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
435	        "parameters": {
436	          "type": "object",
437	          "properties": {
438	            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
439	            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
440	          }
441	        }
442	      }
443	    }
444	  ],
445	  "transitions": [
446	    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
447	  ]
448	}
449	```
450	
451	| Parameter | Meaning |
452	|---|---|
453	| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
454	| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |
455	
456	### Reading and writing variables
457	
458	- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
459	- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
460	- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.
461	
462	Verified in a working builder:
463	
464	- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
465	- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
466	- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
467	- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
468	- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.
469	
470	### What a code node returns
471	
472	Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is
473	
474	```json
475	{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
476	```
477	
478	The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:
479	
480	| Variable | Value |
481	|---|---|
482	| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
483	| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
484	| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
485	| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
486	| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
487	| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
488	| `setup_success_count` | `1` |
489	
490	For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.
491	
492	### Rules for snippets
493	
494	- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
495	- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
496	- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
497	- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
498	- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
499	- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.
500	
501	### Sandbox limits
502	
503	| Limit | Value |
504	|---|---|
505	| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
506	| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
507	| Network and file access | Not documented |
508	| Memory and output size | Not documented |
509	
510	### `code_exec` as a tool
511	
512	`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.
513	
514	## Lifecycle tools
515	
516	A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.
517	
518	| Value | When |
519	|---|---|
520	| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
521	| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
522	| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |
523	
524	Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.
525	
526	```json
527	{
528	  "initial_node": "greeting",
529	  "nodes": {},
530	  "tools": [
531	    {
532	      "type": "function",
533	      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
534	      "function": {
535	        "name": "push_call_result",
536	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
537	        "parameters": {
538	          "type": "object",
539	          "properties": {
540	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
541	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
542	            "body": {
543	              "type": "object",
544	              "properties": {
545	                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
546	                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
547	              }
548	            }
549	          }
550	        }
551	      }
552	    }
553	  ]
554	}
555	```
556	
557	Rules:
558	
559	- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
560	- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
561	- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
562	- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
563	- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
564	- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).
565	
566	## Tool results and the next turn
567	
568	After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:
569	
570	- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
571	- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.
572	
573	What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.
574	
575	Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.
576	
577	## Checklist
578	
579	- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
580	- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
581	- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
582	- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
583	- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
584	- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
585	- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
586	- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
587	- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.
588
